identity: Zoologist and women's rights activist · Brazil · 1894–1976
title: Bertha Lutz's birth chart
metaDescription: Bertha Lutz's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 10.3° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 10.3° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 10.3° Leo — deep enough in the second decan (10°–20°) that Jupiter, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Cancer (23.8°), Venus in Cancer (9.9°), Mars in Aries (23.1°): thought steeped in tone and memory, attraction that works by atmosphere, effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury and Mars hold the closest angle here — a square, 0.7° wide. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, the Sun square Uranus at 1.1°, and the Sun sextile Pluto at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Every angle named here holds for the whole of that day at the birthplace, so an unknown hour cannot take it away.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mars opposes Saturn while both square Mercury. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags four placements in this chart. The Sun in Leo at 10.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Aries at 23.1° is in domicile; Jupiter in Gemini at 26.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Libra at 19.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 air, 3 water, 2 fire by element and 4 cardinal, 3 mutable, 2 fixed by mode. Air runs on comparison and connection — the pattern noticed first, the feeling filed second. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. The day carried no retrograde motion at all; everything moved forward as seen from here.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Leo into Virgo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 15.0° between one midnight and the next. Which of the two it was depends entirely on the hour, and the hour is not recorded. Rather than pick the likelier half, the reading leaves the Moon open.
